scope: Implement and fast-validate the ODA v5.4.1 R2018 outer annotative-data branch for multiline ATTRIB/ATTDEF while preserving separate nested-MTEXT state and refusing unsupported DXF projection.

observed: ATTRIB and ATTDEF models carry separate outer annotative bytes, the associated unknown BS value, the registered-application numeric handle, and a separate APPID-name identity; copy/move/assignment/reset preserve or clear these fields.

AC1032 ATTRIB type 2 and ATTDEF type 4 parsers consume bounded conditional outer payload and hard-pointer data separately from embedded MTEXT; wrong sibling type and malformed/truncated framing fail closed.
DWG encoders emit the conditional size/payload/unknown value and registered-application hard pointer before style handle, and reject the state on older targets or incompatible attribute types.

The DWG reader resolves the source hard-pointer through the parsed APPID table. The R2007+ writer maps the APPID name to the emitted APPID handle and restores the caller's source numeric handle after encoding.

Generated full DWG round-trip asserts ATTRIB and ATTDEF APPID name/target identity, following-record alignment, style/prompt and flags/lock. A missing output APPID causes destination-preserving refusal.
The object-vector target asserts ATTRIB/ATTDEF copy construction, assignment, move, nested-MTEXT deep copy, and reset of the complete outer annotation state.
ASCII and binary DXF export refuses this DWG-only outer state before publishing output instead of silently dropping the payload.
limitations: No real AC1032 producer drawing or independent reader/consumer was available; generated writer/readback controls establish local behavior only.
A malformed full-file case with the outer hard pointer aimed at a non-APPID object has not been injected with enclosing integrity fields recomputed.
No claim is made for native CAD acceptance, complete multiline attributes, or general DWG/DXF support.
